jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**
-------------------


Gastronomous is hiring its first full\-time Head of Finance, an executive role spanning finance and operations. You will sit at the executive table, report to the CEO, attend our quarterly board meetings, and build the financial backbone of a robotics company in the middle of a major scale\-up.


This role keeps the books, and goes far beyond them. You will be a leader and a champion of our growth: shaping pricing, steering the finances of our operation, raising capital and helping take us into new countries. The role is built to grow into CFO after our Series A.

**Head of Finance** · Oakville, Ontario (on\-site) · Full\-time, permanent

**About Gastronomous**
----------------------


We are building the “Kitchen of the Future (https://youtu.be/DFROAGdIar4?si\=9mDdiQYygplqu5KF)” for quick\-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI\-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open\-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.


**How we work.** We are a no\-nonsense team of passionate, execution\-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

**How fast we are growing.** The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

* **Purchase orders signed with major brands**, moving us from pilots to rollout
* **A new office in La Mirada, California** to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
* **Our own ERP**, built in\-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing


The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

**Why This Role**
-----------------

* **A seat at the executive table.** You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
* **In the boardroom.** You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade\-offs to our directors and investors.
* **Champion our growth.** Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
* **Breadth few finance roles offer.** Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
* **Build it from the ground up.** Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new\-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
* **A path to CFO.** This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
* **A team behind you.** You start with a full\-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------


Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

### ***1\. Lead the finance function***


You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

* **Close and reporting.** Lead the month\-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
* **Year\-end.** Lead year\-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year\-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
* **Budget and forecasts.** Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
* **Revenue and billing.** Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
* **Accounts receivable.** Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
* **Tax, audit and compliance.** Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
* **Payroll and benefits.** Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost\-effective.
* **SR\&ED and government funding.** Assist with preparing our SR\&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
* **Systems and day\-to\-day accounting.** Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands\-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.

### ***2\. Drive the financial side of our operations***

* **Pricing and margins.** Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract\-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
* **Inventory and systems.** Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in\-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
* **US operations.** Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
* **Cash and financing.** Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing.

jobs.title: Director, Financial Performance & Efficiency
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 279233
  

  

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high\-performing culture.

  

Scotiabank's Global Technology Enterprise Platforms (GTEP) provides secure, resilient and efficient technology infrastructure that enable the Bank's business strategy and customer experience. The Strategic Portfolio Office (SPO) supports GTEP leadership through integrated strategy, financial management, performance transparency, portfolio governance and enterprise\-wide transformation.

  

The **Director, Financial Performance \& Efficiency** is responsible for leading the financial performance management and efficiency agenda across GTEP. The role provides an integrated view of financial results, outlook, productivity and value delivery, enabling leaders to make timely, fact\-based decisions and deliver against financial commitments.

  

The role is accountable for strengthening planning, forecasting, performance reporting and cost governance; identifying and advancing sustainable efficiency opportunities; and translating financial and operational information into clear executive insights. This includes partnering across GTEP, Finance, Procurement and other stakeholders to improve transparency, accountability and execution.

  

**Is this role right for you? In this role you will:**

  

* Financial Planning \& Performance Management
	+ Lead integrated financial planning, forecasting and performance management across GTEP, aligning financial commitments with strategic priorities and delivery plans.
	+ Establish a clear and consistent view of actuals, outlook, variances, risks and opportunities, with defined ownership and actions to close performance gaps.
	+ Develop executive\-level reporting and insights that connect financial results with operational drivers, investment choices and business outcomes.
	+ Strengthen financial governance, management routines and decision support to improve predictability, transparency and accountability.

* Efficiency \& Value Optimization
	+ Define and advance the GTEP efficiency agenda, including sustainable cost reduction, demand management, productivity improvement and reinvestment opportunities.
	+ Identify, assess and prioritize efficiency opportunities using financial, operational and benchmark information; establish baselines, targets, benefits and delivery plans.
	+ Track realized and forecast benefits, challenge delivery gaps and ensure efficiency commitments are supported by credible actions and evidence.
	+ Promote disciplined cost management and value\-based decision making across the organization without compromising resilience, risk management or service outcomes.

* Governance, Reporting \& Insights
	+ Own the financial performance and efficiency reporting framework, including measures, definitions, data quality standards, controls and executive reporting cadence.
	+ Provide concise, forward\-looking insights and recommendations to GTEP leaders, highlighting material trends, trade\-offs, decisions and required interventions.
	+ Improve the consistency and usability of management information by simplifying reporting, reducing manual effort and enabling greater automation where appropriate.
	+ Support leadership forums, planning cycles and portfolio reviews with decision\-ready analysis and clear accountability for follow\-through.

* Leadership \& Stakeholder Management
	+ Build trusted partnerships with GTEP leaders, Finance, Procurement, workforce teams, portfolio owners and other enterprise stakeholders.
	+ Influence senior stakeholders to align financial choices, operational priorities and efficiency actions with GTEP and Bank objectives.
	+ Foster a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, collaboration, continuous improvement and measurable value delivery.
	+ Lead, coach and develop a high\-performing team with strong capabilities in financial management, analytics, business advisory and executive communication.

**Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have:**

  

* University degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline; a professional accounting or finance designation is an asset.
* 10\+ years of progressive experience in financial management, business performance, strategic planning, cost optimization, technology finance or a related field within a large, complex organization.
* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise\-scale planning, forecasting, management reporting and efficiency programs.
* Strong financial acumen with the ability to connect financial results to operational drivers, strategic choices and measurable business outcomes.
* Advanced analytical and problem\-solving skills, with experience translating complex data into clear executive insights and recommendations.
* Experience establishing performance measures, financial governance, benefit tracking and management routines that improve accountability and execution.
* Strong stakeholder management, influencing and executive communication capabilities, including the ability to constructively challenge senior leaders.
* Demonstrated leadership experience building and developing high\-performing teams in a matrixed enterprise environment.
* Knowledge of technology infrastructure, enterprise platforms, financial services or regulated environments is an asset.

  

**What's in it for you?**

  

* Diversity, Equity, Inclusion \& Allyship \- We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias\-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow \& participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability \& veterans.
* Acces

jobs.title: Site Finance Leader
jobs.description:
Eaton’s Electrical sector is currently seeking a Site Finance Leader to join our CPDI team. This hybrid position is based at our Toronto, ON facility and offers benefits from day one.

 *The expected annual salary range for this role is $93000 \- $117000 a year.*

*Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*


**What you’ll do:**
-------------------



The Site Finance Manager provides direct financial leadership for the Critical Power and Digital Infrastructure business unit, serving as a strategic business partner and change agent to drive continuous improvement and achieve overall business objectives.


This role partners closely with Operations, Sales, Service, and Supply Chain teams to provide financial guidance and actionable insights, drive accountability, and help ensure business strategies and decisions deliver the expected financial and operational results.

 **Key responsibilities include:**

* Analyze financial data and operational performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement. Partner with operational leaders to establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and drive accountability for results.
* Provide financial insights and analysis to support business decision\-making, including capital investment opportunities and resource prioritization.
* Drive productivity and profitability through operational excellence, effective supply chain management, and disciplined budget management across the region.
* Build organizational capability across both sites by supporting talent development, organizational design, and succession planning.
* Partner with Operations to develop action plans, strategies, and initiatives based on financial insights. Monitor execution and measure results through appropriate KPIs.
* Develop financial models and scenario analyses to assess potential impacts on operational and financial performance.
* Identify financial and operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
* Monitor and manage operational costs to improve efficiency and reduce costs while maintaining quality and business performance.
* Lead inventory control actions and initiatives to improve operational profitability and optimize cash flow.
* Coordinate profit planning and forecasting activities, including analysis of key operational metrics and manufacturing costs.
* Lead the planning and deployment of capital investments to support short\-, medium\-, and long\-term business needs. Ensure capital is appropriately prioritized and allocated based on business requirements and cash flow.
* Guide sites through Finance Transformation initiatives, including leading change management efforts and implementing best practices that strengthen financial and operational performance.
**Qualifications:**
-------------------


**Basic Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressive accounting, finance, or controllership experience.
* Minimum of 3 years of experience in an operations or manufacturing environment.
* Must be legally authorized to work in Canada without company sponsorship now or in the future.
* No relocation is offered.
 **Preferred Qualifications:**

* CPA designation or actively pursuing a CPA designation. CFA or other relevant professional financial designation is considered an asset.
* Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Sarbanes\-Oxley (SOX) requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with financial and data analytics, including translating complex financial information into actionable business insights.
* Knowledge of Canadian federal and provincial tax laws and regulations.
* Understanding of foreign currency transactions, translation, and financial reporting requirements.
* Experience with Oracle Financials or similar ERP systems, including financial system integration.
* Strong knowledge of internal controls, financial governance, and risk management.
* Experience supporting financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and manufacturing cost analysis.
* Experience partnering with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, or other cross\-functional teams in a manufacturing environment.
**What makes you successful:**
------------------------------


You’re a collaborative and proactive finance professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful business insights. You communicate financial concepts in a clear and practical way, build trusted relationships across teams, and are comfortable working in a fast\-paced, matrixed environment. You bring strong analytical and Excel skills, manage priorities effectively, and enjoy staying connected to the business by partnering closely with manufacturing teams, including spending time on the shop floor and occasionally visiting other sites.  

All positions may require participation in video and in\-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job\-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

  

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

  



At Eaton we leverage artificial intelligence to recommend jobs to you that match the skills and experience required for the open role. Our Talent Acquisition teams also uses AI to identify applicants whose skills are a match for the job. Hiring decisions are made by Eaton leaders through a structured interview process and not AI.

jobs.title: Director, Growth Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
**Reporting to:** Chief Growth Officer

**Years of experience:** 8\+ years


**Location:** This role is based in Toronto and follows a hybrid work arrangement, with three days per week in the Toronto office and the remaining workdays remote.

**Position type:** Full\-time

**Working conditions:** Regular collaboration across global time zones and international travel up to 20% of working time, are required.

**About Raising The Village**


Raising The Village's mission is to build and strengthen pathways out of ultra\-poverty through an approach guided by data, designed with communities, and scaled by partnerships. We work with last\-mile communities to implement solutions that raise incomes, sustain impact, and chart sustainable pathways to possibility within 24 months. To date, we have supported more than two million people in Uganda, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, with support from our partners and our team in North America. Find out more about our programs and impact at www.raisingthevillage.org (http://www.raisingthevillage.org/).


**Position overview**


Raising The Village is building a Growth function capable of supporting a much larger and more diversified philanthropic portfolio. The Director, Growth Operations \& Strategy will lead the Partnerships Hub—the team that provides the systems, intelligence, writing, stewardship support, and execution capacity behind RTV's fundraising efforts. Reporting directly to the Chief Growth Officer, this leader will translate ambitious growth priorities into practical operating plans, reliable revenue intelligence, strong grant compliance oversight, and seamless cross\-functional delivery. The role is ideal for a builder who enjoys fast\-moving environments, can create clarity amid change, and is equally comfortable setting direction and rolling up their sleeves to make things work.


**Key responsibilities**

*Lead and build the Partnerships Hub*

* Build, lead, and develop a high\-performing team spanning stakeholder experience and stewardship, philanthropic intelligence and research, philanthropic writing and reporting, and administrative support; sequence hiring and clarify responsibilities as the Hub grows.
* Establish priorities, service standards, capacity plans, and clear handoffs so the Hub provides responsive, high\-quality support to the CGO, senior fundraisers, and CEO\-led relationships.
* Coach managers, remove execution barriers, and create a culture of ownership, constructive problem\-solving, and continuous improvement.

*Growth operations, forecasting, and decision support*

* Serve as a strategic operating partner to the CGO, translating revenue and portfolio priorities into actionable plans, performance measures, and operating rhythms.
* Own fundraising pipeline governance and forecasting processes, including opportunity definitions, stage discipline, data quality, scenario analysis, and clear visibility into revenue risks and opportunities.
* Develop dashboards and management reporting on pipeline health, forecast reliability, renewals, funding concentration, grant commitments, and Hub performance; surface insights and recommend action.
* Partner closely with Finance to reconcile forecasts, grant commitments, revenue recognition inputs, and cash receipts, with clear definitions and ownership across systems.

*Fundraising systems and scalable processes*

* Set the strategy for Salesforce and connected fundraising tools; ensure reliable records, useful workflows, and consistent team adoption.
* Lead improvements to Salesforce configuration, reporting, automations, and integrations, delivering routine changes internally where skills and system complexity allow and managing technical partners for more specialized configurations.
* Oversee reliable donation data flows between online giving tools, Salesforce, and Finance, with appropriate reconciliation, exception handling, and data\-quality controls.
* Design and continuously improve processes for opportunity handoffs, proposals, donor reporting, renewals, information requests, and stewardship execution; automate repetitive work when possible.

*Grants operations, compliance, and cross\-functional execution*

* Establish a consistent grant\-operations framework covering contract negotiation, restricted funding terms, activity/milestone tracking, reporting deadlines, amendments, closeout, and documentation throughout.
* Ensure each grant has clear accountable owners, a practical compliance checklist, timely escalation of risks, and an auditable record of key decisions and donor approvals.
* Coordinate with Finance, Legal, Programs, and Impact teams to align grant commitments with financial and programmatic delivery, while preserving those teams' ownership of spending controls, technical results, and evidence validation.
* Oversee cross\-functional execution of major funding opportunities and donor commitments, ensuring the right specialists contribute at the right time without pulling senior relationship managers into routine project management.
* Partner with Communications and the Hub's specialist managers to streamline access to approved program information and reusable content, minimizing duplicate requests to country teams.

**What success looks like**

* The CGO and senior fundraisers spend more of their time on relationships and revenue generation and less time chasing inputs, deadlines, and operational details.
* Leadership has a trustworthy view of the pipeline, forecasts, renewals, and portfolio risks, with clear actions arising from the data.
* Grant obligations and deadlines are consistently tracked; issues are surfaced early; donor\-facing deliverables move smoothly across teams.
* Salesforce and related systems are dependable, appropriately configured, and continuously improving without unnecessary reliance on external implementers.

**Join the EDC Team!**


At EDC, we support Canadian businesses to succeed globally. We provide the financial tools and expertise they need to explore new markets, reduce risks, all towards the goal of making Canada and the world better through trade.


**Position:** Director, Structured and Project Finance \- Infrastructure

**Employment Type:** Permanent

**Compensation Details:** Director, Underwriter 22: Salaries typically range from $178,118 to $237,490 annually, based on qualifications and experiences, plus a performance\-based incentive.


**Location:**

* Export Development Canada operates under a hybrid work model. As of September 2026, our in\-office requirement has increased to three days per week and will be implemented gradually through a phased approach based on employee location. (subject to change).
* This role is expected to be based at EDC’s Headquarters in Ottawa. Candidates located near EDC’s Toronto or Montreal offices will also be considered.
* Relocation assistance to Ottawa will be made available for candidates who meet the eligibility criteria.

*Internal Employees, please consult the ServiceNow article entitled Internal movements – what you need to know.*

**About EDC:**


At Export Development Canada (EDC), we empower Canadian businesses to succeed globally. As a financial Crown corporation, we offer innovative financial solutions and expert insights to help businesses explore new markets, mitigate risks, and achieve growth.

* Comprehensive Benefits: EDC offers a competitive compensation \& benefits package, work\-life balance, \& the opportunity to help make Canada and the world better through trade.

Over the years, EDC’s Structured and Project Finance team has built a significant portfolio across different industries, like mining and metals, infrastructure, telecommunications, energy, renewables, and clean technology.


Structured and Project Finance is a specialized field of finance, in which financing decisions are based upon project\-specific cash flow and assets. Generally speaking, these transactions tend to be large and complex. Counterparties to EDC's Structured and Project Finance transactions include top\-tier Canadian and international sponsors, exporters, law firms and international Project Finance and investment banks.

jobs.title: Director, Total Compensation and HR Data
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

VOSKER is a North American leader in remote area surveillance.


Every day, we’re proud to help our customers keep an eye on what truly matters to them by developing solar\-powered, cellular\-connected cameras integrated with our exclusive platform.


In a few words, at VOSKER: we perform, we think differently, and we take care of our people. We leverage our expertise to win as a team and redefine what’s possible!


WHAT WE OFFER

* A work environment where your ideas come to life and your ambitions take flight
* A dynamic, non\-routine daily life every day is different, and that’s what makes it exciting!
* A hybrid work model: work from home or from one of our offices it’s your choice
* The opportunity to work remotely from abroad for up to 3 months (90 days)
* Access to a learning platform to grow your skills on company time
* A wellness account to reimburse expenses related to your health, passions, and interests
* Free 24/7 access to online healthcare professionals and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Comprehensive group insurance including vision and dental, 50% paid by the employer
* A group RRSP with employer contributions
* Parental leave top\-up for new parents
* Vacation based on your total years of professional experience

  

**Job Description**  

Fair compensation, benefits that make a difference in our people’s lives, and data that informs decisions: at VOSKER, you’ll have the chance to shape all of this.


As the head of total compensation and reporting to the Head of Culture and Organizational Performance, you’ll be a trusted partner in a role that’s both strategic and highly hands\-on. If you enjoy influencing decisions without losing sight of the big picture, this position is for you.

  

WHAT’S IN STORE FOR YOU:

* Compensation: Define and implement VOSKER’s compensation policies in the context of growth and the integration of current (Estonia or Germany) or future acquisitions.
* Business Partnership: Support the teams’ needs regarding salary recommendations, salary benchmarking, annual raises, bonus plans and long\-term incentive programs, pay equity, and business intelligence.
* Employee Benefits and Savings: Develop our programs, negotiate contracts, and manage external partners (Dialogue, Industrielle Alliance, Solertia, etc.) .
* Data and HRIS: Analyze and share key metrics with the Talent \& Culture team and senior management. Support the systems administration team in governing T\&C data via the HRIS (UKG Pro) and oversee the deployment of new HRIS modules as needed.
* Mergers and Acquisitions: Participate in due diligence and the integration of upcoming projects.
* Budget: Participate in establishing annual payroll and benefits budgets with the Finance team.
* Promoting the Value Proposition: Collaborate with colleagues in the Culture Promotion team to foster transparency and highlight the value proposition to employees.
* Leadership and Strategic Oversight: Motivate and guide the total compensation team and its members, while staying abreast of emerging market trends and compensation governance practices.

 **Qualifications** **Key Qualifications**

* You hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources management, finance, actuarial science, or any other relevant field.
* You have held a strategic position in compensation management for at least 7 years, with solid knowledge of employee benefits, long\-term incentive plans, and retirement savings.
* You are comfortable taking on a cross\-functional role that involves frequent and complex collaboration with various departments.
* You have a strong ability to influence both senior management and the entire workforce, and you can communicate the company’s compensation vision in both French and English (written and oral).
* You want to play a strategic role while remaining firmly grounded in hands\-on work and execution.

**Plus Points**

* You have experience in an international environment and in integrating new entities following acquisitions (strongly preferred).
* You are committed to delivering a distinctive employee experience and find creative solutions to the situations that arise.
* You have a good sense of humor and the desire to take on this very serious role without taking yourself too seriously!

**WHAT WE OFFER**

* A high\-impact role in a fast\-growing company, at the heart of integrating new teams across Europe.
* An international setting and a variety of challenges: compensation, benefits, data, and onboarding.
* A culture where we take our work seriously, but not ourselves.
* A hybrid work model that involves working in downtown Montreal at least once a week, occasionally in Victoriaville, and from home on other days.

  

**Additional Information** **EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**


At VOSKER, we value the uniqueness of every individual and celebrate the diversity that helps us redefine what’s possible. We foster collaboration in a healthy, inclusive work environment where all voices are heard.


If you have specific needs to make the recruitment process more accessible, don’t hesitate to reach out.


Now it’s your turn, tell us about yourself and apply today

**Company Description**  

VOSKER is a North American leader in remote area surveillance.


Every day, we’re proud to help our customers keep an eye on what truly matters to them by developing solar\-powered, cellular\-connected cameras integrated with our exclusive platform.


In a few words, at VOSKER: we perform, we think differently, and we take care of our people. We leverage our expertise to win as a team and redefine what’s possible!


WHAT WE OFFER

* A work environment where your ideas come to life and your ambitions take flight
* A dynamic, non\-routine daily life every day is different, and that’s what makes it exciting!
* A hybrid work model: work from home or from one of our offices it’s your choice
* The opportunity to work remotely from abroad for up to 3 months (90 days)
* Access to a learning platform to grow your skills on company time
* A wellness account to reimburse expenses related to your health, passions, and interests
* Free 24/7 access to online healthcare professionals and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Comprehensive group insurance including vision and dental, 50% paid by the employer
* A group RRSP with employer contributions
* Parental leave top\-up for new parents
* Vacation based on your total years of professional experience

  

**Job Description**  

Fair compensation, benefits that make a difference in our people’s lives, and data that informs decisions: at VOSKER, you’ll have the chance to shape all of this.


As the head of total compensation and reporting to the Head of Culture and Organizational Performance, you’ll be a trusted partner in a role that’s both strategic and highly hands\-on. If you enjoy influencing decisions without losing sight of the big picture, this position is for you.

  

WHAT’S IN STORE FOR YOU:

* Compensation: Define and implement VOSKER’s compensation policies in the context of growth and the integration of current (Estonia or Germany) or future acquisitions.
* Business Partnership: Support the teams’ needs regarding salary recommendations, salary benchmarking, annual raises, bonus plans and long\-term incentive programs, pay equity, and business intelligence.
* Employee Benefits and Savings: Develop our programs, negotiate contracts, and manage external partners (Dialogue, Industrielle Alliance, Solertia, etc.) .
* Data and HRIS: Analyze and share key metrics with the Talent \& Culture team and senior management. Support the systems administration team in governing T\&C data via the HRIS (UKG Pro) and oversee the deployment of new HRIS modules as needed.
* Mergers and Acquisitions: Participate in due diligence and the integration of upcoming projects.
* Budget: Participate in establishing annual payroll and benefits budgets with the Finance team.
* Promoting the Value Proposition: Collaborate with colleagues in the Culture Promotion team to foster transparency and highlight the value proposition to employees.
* Leadership and Strategic Oversight: Motivate and guide the total compensation team and its members, while staying abreast of emerging market trends and compensation governance practices.

 **Qualifications** **Key Qualifications**

* You hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources management, finance, actuarial science, or any other relevant field.
* You have held a strategic position in compensation management for at least 7 years, with solid knowledge of employee benefits, long\-term incentive plans, and retirement savings.
* You are comfortable taking on a cross\-functional role that involves frequent and complex collaboration with various departments.
* You have a strong ability to influence both senior management and the entire workforce, and you can communicate the company’s compensation vision in both French and English (written and oral).
* You want to play a strategic role while remaining firmly grounded in hands\-on work and execution.

**Plus Points**

* You have experience in an international environment and in integrating new entities following acquisitions (strongly preferred).
* You are committed to delivering a distinctive employee experience and find creative solutions to the situations that arise.
* You have a good sense of humor and the desire to take on this very serious role without taking yourself too seriously!

**WHAT WE OFFER**

* A high\-impact role in a fast\-growing company, at the heart of integrating new teams across Europe.
* An international setting and a variety of challenges: compensation, benefits, data, and onboarding.
* A culture where we take our work seriously, but not ourselves.
* A hybrid work model that involves working in downtown Montreal at least once a week, occasionally in Victoriaville, and from home on other days.

  

**Additional Information** **EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER**


At VOSKER, we value the uniqueness of every individual and celebrate the diversity that helps us redefine what’s possible. We foster collaboration in a healthy, inclusive work environment where all voices are heard.


If you have specific needs to make the recruitment process more accessible, don’t hesitate to reach out.


Now it’s your turn, tell us about yourself and apply today
